source.title: Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible
source.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and David Brown
source.edition: CCEL expanded electronic edition of the 1871 public-domain text

entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: Pr 3:1-35 . The study of truth commended. God must be feared, honored, and trusted, and filial submission, under chastisement, exhibited. The excellence of wisdom urged and illustrated by its place in the divine counsels. Piety enforced by a contrast of the destiny of the righteous and the wicked.

entries.heading: 2. length . . . life
entries.text: 2. length . . . life --often promised as blessings ( Ps 21:4; 91:16 ). peace --includes prosperity ( Ps 125:5 ). add --abound to thee.

entries.heading: 3. mercy and truth
entries.text: 3. mercy and truth --God's faithfulness to His promises is often expressed by these terms ( Ps 25:10; 57:3 ). As attributes of men, they express integrity in a wide sense ( Pr 16:6; 20:28 ). bind . . . write . . . heart --outwardly adorn and inwardly govern motives.

entries.heading: 4. favour
entries.text: 4. favour --grace, amiability ( Pr 22:11; Ps 45:2 ); united with this, a good understanding --(Compare Margin ), a discrimination, which secures success. in the sight . . . man --such as God and man approve.

entries.heading: 5. Trust . . . heart
entries.text: 5. Trust . . . heart --This is the center and marrow of true wisdom ( Pr 22:19; 28:25 ). The positive duty has its corresponding negation in the admonition against self-confidence.

entries.heading: 6. ways
entries.text: 6. ways -- ( Ps 1:1 ). acknowledge --by seeking His wise aid ( Pr 16:3; Ps 37:5; Jer 9:23, 24 ). direct --literally, "make plain" (compare Heb 12:13 ).
7. (Compare Pr 27:2; Ro 12:16 ). fear . . . evil --reverentially regarding His law.

entries.heading: 8. It
entries.text: 8. It --This conduct. health --(Compare Margin ). to thy navel --for all the organs of nourishment. marrow --(Compare Margin ). bones --frame of body. True piety promotes bodily health.

entries.heading: 10. presses
entries.text: 10. presses --or wine fats ( Joe 2:24; 3:13 ).
11, 12. The true intent of afflictions considered; they do not contradict the assertion of the blessed state of the pious ( Job 5:17; Heb 12:5, 6 ).

entries.heading: 12. he delighteth
entries.text: 12. he delighteth --or receiveth as denoting reconciliation regarding the offense which produced chastisement.

entries.heading: 13. findeth
entries.text: 13. findeth --literally, "reaches," or "obtains by seeking." getteth --literally, "draws out," as metals by digging.
14, 15. The figure of Pr 3:13 carried out. it --that is, wisdom. merchandise of silver --acquisition by trading. fine gold --dug gold, solid as a nugget.

entries.heading: 15. rubies
entries.text: 15. rubies --gems, or pearls.
16, 17. Wisdom personified as bringing the best blessings (compare Mt 6:33; 1Ti 4:8 ).

entries.heading: 17. Her ways
entries.text: 17. Her ways --such as she directs us to take.
18. Wisdom allegorized as a tree of life -- ( Ge 2:9; 3:22 ) whose fruit preserves life, gives all that makes living a blessing.

19, 20. The place of wisdom in the economy of creation and providence commends it to men, who, in proportion to their finite powers, may possess this invaluable attribute, and are thus encouraged by the divine example of its use to seek its possession.

entries.heading: 21. sound wisdom
entries.text: 21. sound wisdom --(compare Pr 2:7 ). let . . . eyes --that is, these words of instruction.
22-24. assign reasons in their value for happiness and ornament, guidance and support in dangers, both when waking and sleeping.

entries.heading: 25. Be not
entries.text: 25. Be not --or, "You shall not be." sudden fear --what causes it ( Pr 1:27 ), any unlooked-for evil ( Ps 46:3; 91:12; 1Pe 3:14 ). desolation -- ( Pr 1:27 ).
26. The reason; such as are objects of God's favor. be thy confidence --literally, "in thy confidence," in the source of thy strength (compare Na 3:9 , for the same construction, Hebrew ).
27, 28. Promptly fulfil all obligations both of justice and charity (compare Jas 2:15, 16 ).
29, 30. Do not abuse confidence and avoid litigation.

entries.heading: 31. oppressor
entries.text: 31. oppressor --or man of mischief. The destiny of successful evildoers warns against desiring their lot ( Ps 37:1, 2, 35, 36 ).
32-35. Reasons for the warning. froward -- ( Pr 2:15 ). secret . . . righteous --in their communion ( Am 3:7 ).

entries.heading: 33. curse . . . wicked
entries.text: 33. curse . . . wicked --It abides with them, and will be manifested.
34. The retribution of sinners, as in Ps 18:26 .

entries.heading: 35. inherit
entries.text: 35. inherit --as a portion. shame --or disgrace, as opposed to honor. promotion --(Compare Margin ); as honor for well-doing makes men conspicuous, so fools are signalized by disgrace.
